fixes.explanation: Nice try, friend, but the seed doesn't work that way. Paul says "Whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and whoever sows generously will also reap generously." So the two harvests are not the same. Each one follows what was sown.

That's right, baker. Paul says each one should give what he has decided in his heart, "…not out of regret or compulsion." That's his instruction: no pressure and no regret. The choice starts in the heart.
That's the one. Paul says, "For God loves a cheerful giver." Cheerful is the word he picks, friend. That's the kind of giver Paul points to when he says to give from the heart.
I would love an overflow of rest, believe me. I've napped on a flour sack or two. But Paul says they "…will abound in every good work." The grace is for doing good.

Ooh, not this time, friend! Read that quote again: "He has scattered abroad His gifts to the poor; His righteousness endures forever." See where those gifts land? The poor. Paul says it right there, so no trick in this one.

Good guess, friend, and I can see why it came to mind. But that word isn't in this verse. Paul says "…through us your generosity will produce thanksgiving to God." Thanksgiving is what the generosity produces.

I got my name carved on a handle, so I know names matter to people. But Paul doesn't say this one. The saints will glorify God "…for your obedient confession of the gospel of Christ…" That's the other thing they glorify God for.
